text:
sophia: quick preflight for aurora-13b private deploy — weights landed, tokenizer quirk spotted, and serving/batching/caching knobs to lock before canary. PTAL @liam @anya @jordan

liam: confirmed weights at s3://redwood-weights/aurora/13b/v1/ (sha256: 9f3a7c...). pulled locally and ran checksum. set WEIGHTS_PATH to that S3 uri for local smoke.

liam: small helper if you need to pull and validate locally:
```bash
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-weights/aurora/13b/v1/model.ckpt ./model.ckpt
sha256sum model.ckpt | grep 9f3a7c
```

anya: heads-up — tokenizer maps trailing newlines inconsistently. decode(encode("hello\n")) sometimes drops the final newline token id on our variant, which breaks prefix cache keys (kv cache mismatch on resume). repro:
```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
t=Tokenizer.from_file("tokenizers/aurora-tokenizer.json")
print(t.encode("hello\n").ids)
```
I can push a normalization fix to the tokenizer config (map \n -> <NL> token) — will open PR.

jordan: for batching/scheduler: what's our target max_tokens_per_request for canary? model ctx is 8192 but we still want to cap per-request to protect scheduler. I suggest 1024 for initial canary, batch_size 16, latency SLO 100ms. Thoughts? :eyes:

sophia: agreed on conservative defaults. here's the proposed preflight serving config (will drop into infra later):
```json
{
  "continuous_batching": {
    "enabled": true,
    "max_batch_size": 16,
    "max_latency_ms": 100,
    "max_concurrent_requests": 4
  },
  "caching_policy": {
    "prefix_cache_enabled": true,
    "prefix_cache_ttl_seconds": 300,
    "max_prefix_length_tokens": 64
  },
  "scheduler": {
    "max_tokens_per_slot": 1024,
    "slot_duration_ms": 50
  },
  "model": {
    "weights_path": "s3://redwood-weights/aurora/13b/v1/",
    "context_window": 8192
  }
}
```

deploy-bot: CI preflight checks started for infra/serve-configs/aurora-13b/preflight.json

ci-bot: preflight: tokenizer-normalization-check: FAIL — trailing-newline-stability. See tests/tokenizer/test_newline_stability.py:12

liam: quick workaround to avoid immediate failures: set prefix_cache_ttl_seconds to 0 to disable cache until tokenizer fixed, or set `prefix_cache_enabled: false`. but we'll lose prefix caching gains.

anya: I pushed the tokenizer normalization patch: https://github.com/redwood/serve/pull/3456 — updates token mapping and adds unit test. CI green on my fork. Please review.

liam: re-ran preflight locally with prefix cache disabled and config above (max_tokens 1024) — smoke pass for concurrency; queue depth remains stable under synthetic load.

ci-bot: preflight: config-validation: WARNING — scheduler.max_tokens_per_slot (1024) < model.context_window (8192) — expected but call-site checks ok.

jordan: question — do we want kv-cache persistence on canary? if tokenizer patch lands, kv-consistency is fine. Otherwise better to disable persistence to avoid resume mismatches.

sophia: for canary tonight let's: (1) merge tokenizer PR, (2) deploy config with prefix_cache_enabled: true and ttl 300 only if PR merged, otherwise prefix_cache_enabled: false, (3) keep max_tokens_per_slot 1024 and max_batch_size 16. aiming for canary at 22:00 UTC. if anyone can't make that timeline call it out now. :shipit:

anya: on it — will merge once CI passes here and in mainbot. ping me if you want me to force-merge after eyeballs. :+1:

liam: I'll stub the infra config path and add a short doc note about the tokenizer caveat in infra/serve-configs/aurora-13b/README.md

sophia: thanks all. if we hit a blocker I'll open an incident thread. otherwise i'll post canary start in ~30m. :rocket:
